title.zh: 卷460 列傳二百四十七 左宝贵弟：宝贤 永山 邓世昌 刘步蟾 林泰曾 戴宗骞
title.en: Volume 460 Biographies 247: Zuo Baogui Younger Brother: Bao Xian, Yong Shan, Deng Shichang, Liu Buchan, Lin Taiceng, Dai Zongqian
title.raw: 卷460 列傳二百四十七 左宝贵弟：宝贤 永山 邓世昌 刘步蟾 林泰曾 戴宗骞

sentences.zh: 列傳二百四十七

translations.literal: Biographies, number two hundred forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 247

sentences.zh: 左寶貴弟寶賢等永山鄧世昌劉步蟾林泰曾等戴宗騫

translations.literal: Zuo Baogui; his younger brother Bao Xian and others; Yong Shan; Deng Shichang; Liu Buchan; Lin Taiceng and others; Dai Zongqian.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Baogui (and his younger brother Bao Xian and others), Yong Shan, Deng Shichang, Liu Buchan, Lin Taiceng and others, and Dai Zongqian

sentences.zh: 左寶貴，字冠廷，山東費人。

translations.literal: Zuo Baogui, courtesy name Guanting, a man of Fei in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Baogui, styled Guanting, was a native of Fei County in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，隸江南軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianfeng reign, he was attached to the Jiangnan army.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xianfeng era he served with the Jiangnan forces.

sentences.zh: 嘗令當前敵，陣既接，旗兵中砲，殪，寶貴持其幟衝鋒入，大捷，繇是知名。

translations.literal: Once ordered to face the enemy in the van; when the lines met, the banner soldier was struck by cannon and killed; Baogui seized the standard and charged in at the head; a great victory; from this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: Once placed in the forefront against the enemy, he saw the standard-bearer cut down by cannon fire as battle was joined; Baogui seized the banner and led the charge himself, winning a great victory, and from that day his name was known.

sentences.zh: 獲苗沛霖，克金陵，頻有功。

translations.literal: He captured Miao Peilin, took Jinling, and repeatedly had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He helped capture Miao Peilin, took Nanjing, and won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 後以游擊從僧格林沁討捻，積勳至副將。

translations.literal: Later, as a guerrilla officer he followed Sengge Rinchen in suppressing the Nian, accumulating merit until vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as a guerrilla officer under Sengge Rinchen in the campaign against the Nian rebels, he rose by accumulated merit to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，尚書崇實巡視奉天、吉林，奏自隨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu, Minister Chongshi inspected Fengtian and Jilin and memorialized that he accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu reign, when Minister Chongshi toured Fengtian and Jilin, he memorialized that Baogui accompany him.

sentences.zh: 既至，斬高希珍於土門，誅宋三好於石砬子。

translations.literal: After arriving, he beheaded Gao Xizhen at Tumen and executed Song Sanhao at Shibazi.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he beheaded Gao Xizhen at Tumen and put Song Sanhao to death at Shibazi.

sentences.zh: 邊外東北廟溝金宮四構黨圖大舉，复捕治之，餘燼悉平，賜號鏗色巴圖魯，晉記名提督。

translations.literal: Beyond the border, conspirators at Dongbei Miaogou and Jingongsi plotted a great rising; he again captured and punished them; remaining embers were all pacified; he was granted the title Kense Batulu and promoted to registered nominal provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: When conspirators beyond the border at Dongbei Miaogou and Jingongsi plotted a major uprising, he captured and punished them again until every ember of revolt was extinguished; he was granted the title Kense Batulu and advanced to registered nominal provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 授高州鎮總兵，仍留奉天。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander of the Gaozhou garrison but remained in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commander of the Gaozhou garrison but continued to serve in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 平朝陽教匪，賞黃馬褂、雙眼花翎，駐瀋陽。

translations.literal: He pacified the sect rebels in Chaoyang, was rewarded with the yellow jacket and double-eyed peacock feather, and was stationed at Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the sect rebels in Chaoyang he was rewarded with the yellow riding jacket and double-eyed peacock feather, and took up station at Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 二十年，朝鮮亂起，日本進兵。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, disorder arose in Korea and Japan advanced troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Guangxu, turmoil broke out in Korea and Japan sent troops.

sentences.zh: 朝議既決戰，衛汝貴、馬玉昆、丰紳阿各率所部往御之，寶貴自奉天來會，是為四大軍。

translations.literal: Once the court had decided on war, Wei Rugui, Ma Yukun, and Fengshen'e each led their units to resist; Baogui came from Fengtian to join them — these were the Four Great Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Once the court resolved on war, Wei Rugui, Ma Yukun, and Fengshen'e each led their commands to resist the invader; Baogui came down from Fengtian to join them — the force known as the Four Great Armies.

sentences.zh: 慮海道梗，乃繞道自遼東行，渡鴨綠江入平壤。

translations.literal: Fearing the sea route would be blocked, they took a detour through eastern Liaodong, crossed the Yalu River, and entered Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the sea lanes would be cut, they marched overland through eastern Liaodong, crossed the Yalu, and entered Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 是時葉志超虛飾戰胜狀，電李鴻章入告，遂拜總統諸軍命。

translations.literal: At that time Ye Zhichao falsely reported victories and telegraphed Li Hongzhang; he was then appointed commander-in-chief of all forces.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ye Zhichao dressed up false reports of victory and telegraphed Li Hongzhang with the news, and was accordingly appointed commander-in-chief of all forces.

sentences.zh: 於是汝貴、玉昆軍南門外大同江，志超部將江自康軍北門外小山，寶貴任城守。

translations.literal: Thereupon Rugui's and Yukun's troops were on the Datong River south of the southern gate; Ye Zhichao's subordinate Jiang Zikang's troops on the hill north of the northern gate; Baogui was charged with holding the city.
translations.idiomatic: Rugui and Yukun took position on the Datong River south of the southern gate; Ye Zhichao's subordinate Jiang Zikang held the hill north of the northern gate; and Baogui was charged with defending the city itself.

sentences.zh: 未止舍，日軍猝至，寶貴與丰紳阿擊卻之。

translations.literal: Before they had even settled in camp, Japanese troops suddenly arrived; Baogui and Fengshen'e beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: They had scarcely made camp when Japanese troops struck without warning; Baogui and Fengshen'e drove them back.

sentences.zh: 敵退龍岡，分道來攻，又敗之。

translations.literal: The enemy withdrew to Longgang and attacked by separate routes; they were defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fell back to Longgang and attacked along several routes; they were beaten again.

sentences.zh: 志超乃聚全軍為嬰城計。

translations.literal: Ye Zhichao then gathered the entire army to plan a purely defensive holding of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Zhichao then drew the whole army together to hold the city behind its walls.

sentences.zh: 時寶貴扼玄武門，日軍大隊至。

translations.literal: Baogui then held the Xuanwu Gate when a large Japanese force arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Baogui was holding the Xuanwu Gate when a large Japanese column came up.

sentences.zh: 志超將潰圍北歸，寶貴不從，以兵守志超勿令逸。

translations.literal: Ye Zhichao was about to break out of the encirclement and flee north; Baogui would not agree and stationed troops to watch Ye and prevent his escape.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Zhichao was preparing to break out northward; Baogui refused to go along and posted troops to keep Ye from slipping away.

sentences.zh: 寶貴狃於捕馬賊之功，頗輕敵。

translations.literal: Baogui, accustomed to his successes against horse bandits, rather underestimated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Baogui, overconfident after years of chasing down mounted bandits, took the enemy too lightly.

sentences.zh: 日軍轝砲散置山巔，諜者以告，若弗聞。

translations.literal: The Japanese scattered their siege guns on the mountain peaks; spies reported this, but he seemed not to hear.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese had scattered their field guns on the heights; spies brought word of it, but he acted as though he had not heard.

sentences.zh: 登城指麾，中砲踣，猶能言，及城下，始殞。

translations.literal: He mounted the wall to direct operations, was struck by cannon fire and fell; he could still speak, but only after being carried below the wall did he die.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the wall to direct the defense, was struck down by shellfire, and could still speak; only after he was carried below the wall did he die.

sentences.zh: 其部將負屍開城走，遇日軍，又棄之，於是諸軍皆潰。

translations.literal: His subordinate generals carried his corpse and opened the gates to flee; when they met Japanese troops they abandoned the body, and then all the armies routed.
translations.idiomatic: His officers shouldered his body, opened the gates, and fled; when they ran into Japanese troops they abandoned the corpse, and the whole army collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太子少保，諡忠壯，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，子國楫襲。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang, and awarded a hereditary rank as Commandant of Cavalry with one additional Yun Commandant rank; his son Guoji inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned of his death, he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous name Zhongzhuang (Loyal and Stalwart), and granted a hereditary rank as Commandant of Cavalry with one additional Yun Commandant rank; his son Guoji inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 弟寶賢、寶清先後於直隸、奉天剿匪陣亡。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Bao Xian and Bao Qing successively died in battle while suppressing bandits in Zhili and Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Bao Xian and Bao Qing had earlier fallen in battle while suppressing bandits in Zhili and Fengtian, one after the other.

sentences.zh: 永山，袁氏，漢軍正白旗人，黑龍江駐防，吉林將軍富明阿子，黑龍江將軍壽山弟。

translations.literal: Yong Shan, of the Yuan clan, a Hanjun of the Plain White Banner, garrisoned at Heilongjiang; son of Jilin General Fuming'a and younger brother of Heilongjiang General Shoushan.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Shan, of the Yuan clan, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain White Banner, stationed in the Heilongjiang garrison; he was the son of Jilin General Fuming'a and the younger brother of Heilongjiang General Shoushan.

sentences.zh: 以廕授侍衛，歸東三省練軍。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he was appointed an Imperial Bodyguard and returned to the Three Eastern Provinces training army.
translations.idiomatic: By hereditary privilege he was appointed an Imperial Bodyguard and returned to serve with the training army of the Three Eastern Provinces.

sentences.zh: 中日戰起，從將軍依克唐阿軍，率黑龍江騎旅駐摩天嶺。

translations.literal: When the Sino-Japanese War broke out, he followed General Yiketang'a's army, leading the Heilongjiang cavalry brigade stationed at Motianling.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out between China and Japan, he served under General Yiketang'a, commanding the Heilongjiang cavalry brigade posted at Motianling.

sentences.zh: 永山臨敵輒深入，為士卒先。

translations.literal: Whenever Yong Shan faced the enemy he would press deep into the line, going ahead of his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he met the enemy Yong Shan drove deep into the fight, always ahead of his men.

sentences.zh: 與日軍戰數有功，連殲其將。

translations.literal: In several engagements with the Japanese army he won merit and successively killed many of their officers.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated clashes with the Japanese he distinguished himself and killed several of their officers in succession.

sentences.zh: 既克龍灣，乘勝渡草河，規鳳凰，依克唐阿策襲其城，檄永山為軍鋒，偕壽山分率馬步隊深入攻之。

translations.literal: After capturing Longwan, they took advantage of the victory to cross the Cao River and aimed at Fengcheng; Yiketang'a planned a surprise assault on the city and ordered Yong Shan as the vanguard, together with Shoushan each leading mixed horse and foot columns in a deep attack.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Longwan they pressed the advantage across the Cao River toward Fengcheng; Yiketang'a planned a surprise on the city and named Yong Shan the vanguard, while he and Shoushan each led mixed cavalry and infantry columns in a deep strike.

sentences.zh: 抵一面山，距城八里，張左右翼，各據一坡以待。

translations.literal: They reached Yimianshan, eight li from the city, deployed left and right wings, each occupying a slope in wait.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Yimianshan, eight li from the city, and deployed left and right wings, each holding a slope in readiness.

sentences.zh: 永山為右翼，尤得地勢。

translations.literal: Yong Shan commanded the right wing and especially held the superior terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Shan held the right wing, which had the better ground.

sentences.zh: 敵作散隊，伍伍什什冒死前，復以大隊橫沖我左翼。

translations.literal: The enemy formed skirmish lines, advancing in fives and tens risking death, then sent a large column to charge straight across our left wing.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy came on in open order, advancing in small groups at the risk of their lives, then threw a large column in a slashing charge against our left wing.

sentences.zh: 左翼潰，右翼亦不支，乃相繼退。

translations.literal: The left wing collapsed and the right wing could not hold either, so they withdrew in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The left wing broke, the right could not hold, and the whole line fell back in turn.

sentences.zh: 永山獨為殿，遇伏，連受槍傷，洞胸踣，復強起督戰，大呼殺賊而逝。

translations.literal: Yong Shan alone served as rearguard; ambushed, he received gunshot wounds one after another, was struck through the chest and fell; he forced himself up again to direct the battle, shouted "Kill the bandits!" and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Shan alone covered the retreat; ambushed, he took shot after shot, was pierced through the chest and fell; he dragged himself up to rally the fight, cried "Kill the bandits!" and died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，諡壯愍，予建祠奉天。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, he was given the posthumous name Zhuangmin and a temple was erected for him in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned of his death, he was given the posthumous name Zhuangmin (Stalwart and Sorrowful), and a temple was built for him in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 鄧世昌，字正卿，廣東番禺人。

translations.literal: Deng Shichang, courtesy name Zhengqing, a native of Panyu in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shichang, styled Zhengqing, was a native of Panyu in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 少有幹略，嘗從西人習布算術。

translations.literal: In youth he showed administrative talent and once studied Western bookkeeping under Westerners.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he showed ability and enterprise, and he once studied Western bookkeeping under foreign teachers.

sentences.zh: 既長，入水師學堂，精測量、駕駛。

translations.literal: When grown, he entered the naval academy and mastered surveying and navigation.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he entered the naval academy and mastered surveying and ship handling.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，管海東雲艦，徼循海口。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu, he commanded the coastal ship Haidongyun and patrolled the harbors.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu reign he commanded the Haidongyun and patrolled the coastal harbors.

sentences.zh: 日本窺台灣，扼澎湖、基隆諸隘，補千總，調管振威艦。

translations.literal: When Japan cast covetous eyes on Taiwan and held the passes at Penghu and Keelung, he was appointed thousand-man commander and transferred to command the Zhenwei.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan cast its eye on Taiwan and seized the passes at Penghu and Keelung, he was made a thousand-man commander and transferred to command the Zhenwei.

sentences.zh: 以捕海盜，遷守備。

translations.literal: For capturing pirates he was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing pirates he was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章治海軍，高其能，調北洋。

translations.literal: When Li Hongzhang organized the navy, he valued Shichang's ability and transferred him to the Beiyang Fleet.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang built up the navy, he prized Shichang's ability and transferred him to the Beiyang Fleet.

sentences.zh: 從丁汝昌赴英購鐵艦，益詳練海戰術。

translations.literal: He accompanied Ding Ruchang to England to purchase ironclads and became even more thoroughly versed in naval tactics.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Ding Ruchang to England to buy ironclads and grew thoroughly versed in naval tactics.

sentences.zh: 八年，朝鮮內亂，復從汝昌泊仁川，為吳長慶陸軍後距。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, during internal disorder in Korea, he again followed Ruchang to anchor at Incheon, covering Wu Changqing's land army from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Guangxu, during civil strife in Korea, he again followed Ruchang to anchor at Incheon and covered Wu Changqing's land forces from the sea.

sentences.zh: 事寧，遷游擊，賜號勃勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he was promoted to guerrilla officer and granted the title Boyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis passed he was promoted to guerrilla officer and granted the title Boyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 管揚威快艦，往來天津、朝鮮；

translations.literal: He commanded the fast cruiser Yangwei, traveling between Tianjin and Korea;
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the fast cruiser Yangwei, shuttling between Tianjin and Korea;

sentences.zh: 冬寒冰沍，巡視台、廈海防。

translations.literal: in winter when ice blocked the sea, he patrolled the coastal defenses of Taiwan and Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: and in winter, when the seas froze over, he patrolled the defenses of Taiwan and Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 尋充經遠、致遠、靖遠、濟遠四船營務處，兼致遠管帶。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he joined the fleet staff overseeing the Jingyuan, Zhiyuan, Jingyuan, and Jiyuan, while also commanding the Zhiyuan herself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined the fleet staff overseeing the Jingyuan, Zhiyuan, Jingyuan, and Jiyuan, while also commanding the Zhiyuan herself.

sentences.zh: 十四年，台灣生番畔，以副將從汝昌往討。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when aborigines in Taiwan rebelled, as vice commander he followed Ruchang to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, when the aborigines of Taiwan rose in revolt, he went as vice commander under Ruchang to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 戰埤南，毀其碉寨，擢總兵。

translations.literal: Fighting at Beinan, he destroyed their stockaded forts and was promoted to full commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting at Beinan he destroyed their stockaded forts and was promoted to full commander.

sentences.zh: 時定海軍經制，借補中軍副將，而以汝昌為提督，其左右翼總兵則閩人林泰曾、劉步蟾也。

translations.literal: At that time the navy's permanent establishment was fixed; he was appointed acting central vice commander while Ruchang served as admiral; the left and right wing commanders were the Fujian men Lin Taiceng and Liu Buchan.
translations.idiomatic: When the navy's permanent organization was fixed, he was made acting central vice commander under Admiral Ding Ruchang; the left and right wing commanders were the Fujian men Lin Taiceng and Liu Buchan.

sentences.zh: 汝昌故不習海戰，威令不行。

translations.literal: Ruchang was originally unversed in naval warfare and his authority did not take hold.
translations.idiomatic: Ruchang had never been trained in naval warfare, and his authority did not hold.

sentences.zh: 獨世昌以粵人任管駕，非時不登岸，閩人咸嫉之。

translations.literal: Only Shichang, as a Cantonese holding command of a ship, would not go ashore except when necessary; the Fujian men all envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shichang, a Cantonese in command of a ship, would not leave his vessel except when he had to; the Fujian officers all resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 二十年夏，日侵朝，絕海道。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twentieth year, Japan invaded Korea and cut the sea lanes.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twentieth year Japan invaded Korea and cut the sea lanes.

sentences.zh: 鴻章令濟遠、廣乙兩船赴牙山，遇日艦，先擊，廣乙受殊傷；

translations.literal: Hongzhang ordered the Jiyuan and Guangyi to proceed to Asan; they met Japanese warships and opened fire first; the Guangyi received severe damage;
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang ordered the Jiyuan and Guangyi to Asan; they met Japanese warships and opened fire first; the Guangyi was badly mauled;

sentences.zh: 轟濟遠，都司沈壽昌，守備楊建章、黃承勳中砲死。

translations.literal: they bombarded the Jiyuan; Director Shen Shouchang and Garrison Commanders Yang Jianzhang and Huang Chengxun were killed by cannon fire.
translations.idiomatic: they turned their fire on the Jiyuan; Director Shen Shouchang and Garrison Commanders Yang Jianzhang and Huang Chengxun were killed by shellfire.

sentences.zh: 濟遠逃，日艦追之，管帶方柏謙豎白幟，追益亟，有水手發砲擊之，折日艦了樓，柏謙虛張胜狀，退塞威海東西兩口。

translations.literal: The Jiyuan fled and Japanese warships pursued; Commander Fang Boyian hoisted a white flag, whereupon the pursuit intensified; a sailor fired on them and broke the Japanese ship's signal tower; Boyian falsely claimed victory and withdrew to block the eastern and western entrances to Weihai.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiyuan fled with Japanese ships in pursuit; Commander Fang Boyian ran up a white flag, which only made the pursuit fiercer; a sailor fired back and knocked down the enemy's signal mast; Boyian then falsely claimed a victory and withdrew to block the eastern and western entrances to Weihai.

sentences.zh: 世昌憤欲進兵，汝昌尼其行，不果。

translations.literal: Shichang, indignant, wished to advance; Ruchang restrained him and it did not happen.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang, furious, wanted to advance to the fight, but Ruchang held him back and nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 已而日艦集大連灣，窺金州，我國海軍乃大發，泊鴨綠江大東溝，以鐵艦十當敵艦十有二。

translations.literal: Before long Japanese warships gathered at Dalian Bay and probed Jinzhou; our navy then sortied in force and anchored at Dadonggou on the Yalu, with ten ironclads facing the enemy's twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Japanese ships massed in Dalian Bay and probed Jinzhou; the Chinese navy sortied in force and anchored at Dadonggou on the Yalu, pitting ten ironclads against the enemy's twelve.

sentences.zh: 汝昌乘定遠居中，列諸船左右張兩翼。

translations.literal: Ruchang rode the Dingyuan at the center, arraying the other ships to left and right in two wings.
translations.idiomatic: Ruchang took the Dingyuan at the center and drew up the fleet in two wings to left and right.

sentences.zh: 日艦魚貫進，據上風，汝昌令轟擊，距遠不能中。

translations.literal: Japanese ships advanced in single file, holding the windward position; Ruchang ordered cannon fire, but at too great a distance they could not hit.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese came on in column, holding the weather gauge; Ruchang ordered his guns to fire, but at that range the shots fell short.

sentences.zh: 日艦小，運棹靈，倏分倏合，彈雨坌集，定遠被震，大纛僕。

translations.literal: The Japanese ships were small and maneuvered their oars skillfully, dividing and reuniting in an instant; a rain of shells poured down; the Dingyuan was shaken and its great standard fell.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese ships were smaller and more agile, breaking apart and closing again in an instant; shellfire poured down; the Dingyuan was shaken and her great battle ensign toppled.

sentences.zh: 世昌見帥旗沒，慮軍心搖，亟取致遠纛豎之。

translations.literal: Shichang saw the commander's flag gone and feared the troops' morale would waver; he quickly took the Zhiyuan's standard and raised it.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang saw the admiral's flag gone and feared the fleet's morale would break; he quickly raised the Zhiyuan's ensign in its place.

sentences.zh: 戰良久，定遠擊沉其西京丸，我之超勇毀焉。

translations.literal: After long fighting, the Dingyuan sank their Saikyo Maru, while our Chaoyong was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: After a long fight the Dingyuan sank the Japanese Saikyo Maru, while our own Chaoyong was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 世昌乘致遠，最猛鷙，與日艦吉野浪速相當，吉野，日艦之中堅也。

translations.literal: Shichang rode the Zhiyuan, the fiercest of all, matched against the Japanese Yoshino and Nisshin; the Yoshino was the backbone of the Japanese fleet.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang fought from the Zhiyuan, the fiercest ship in the fleet, matched against the Japanese Yoshino and Nisshin; the Yoshino was the backbone of the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 戰既酣，致遠彈將罄，世昌誓死敵。

translations.literal: When battle grew fierce, the Zhiyuan's ammunition was nearly exhausted; Shichang swore to fight the enemy to the death.
translations.idiomatic: As the fight grew desperate the Zhiyuan's ammunition ran low, and Shichang swore to fight the enemy to the death.

sentences.zh: 將士知大勢敗，陣稍亂，世昌大呼曰：「今日有死而已！

translations.literal: The officers and men, knowing the great situation was lost, the formation grew somewhat disorderly; Shichang shouted loudly: "Today there is nothing but death!
translations.idiomatic: The officers and men, seeing the battle was lost, began to lose formation; Shichang cried out: "Today there is nothing for us but death!

sentences.zh: 然雖死而海軍聲威弗替，是即所以報國也！」

translations.literal: Yet though we die, the navy's prestige shall not fade — that is how we repay the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet if we die, the navy's honor shall not fade — that is how we repay the country!"

sentences.zh: 眾乃定。

translations.literal: The crowd then steadied.
translations.idiomatic: The men steadied at that.

sentences.zh: 世昌遂鼓輪怒駛，欲猛觸吉野與同盡，中其魚雷，鍋船裂沉。

translations.literal: Shichang then drove the screws at full speed in a fury, intending to ram the Yoshino and perish together; he was struck by its torpedo and the boiler ship split apart and sank.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang then drove the Zhiyuan at full speed, intending to ram the Yoshino and go down with her; a torpedo from the Japanese ship struck home, and the Zhiyuan broke apart and sank.

sentences.zh: 世昌身環氣圈不沒，汝昌及他將見之，令馳救。

translations.literal: Shichang's body was ringed by an air pocket and did not sink; Ruchang and the other commanders saw this and ordered a rescue boat sent at speed.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang was caught in an air pocket and did not sink; Ruchang and the other commanders saw him and ordered a boat to hurry to his rescue.

sentences.zh: 拒弗上，縮臂出圈，死之。

translations.literal: He refused to board, drew his arm out of the pocket, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to be pulled aboard, slipped his arm from the air pocket, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 其副游擊陳金揆同殉，全船二百五十人無逃者。

translations.literal: His deputy guerrilla officer Chen Jin'kui died with him; of the whole ship's two hundred fifty men, none fled.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Chen Jin'kui died with him; of the ship's company of two hundred fifty, not one tried to escape.

sentences.zh: 經遠管帶總兵林永昇、超勇管帶參將黃建寅、揚威管帶參將林履中並殞於陣。

translations.literal: Jingyuan commander Commander Lin Yongsheng, Chaoyong commander Major Huang Jianyin, and Yangwei commander Major Lin Lüzhong all fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yongsheng, commander of the Jingyuan; Huang Jianyin, commander of the Chaoyong; and Lin Lüzhong, commander of the Yangwei — all fell in the same battle.

sentences.zh: 事聞，世昌諡壯節，餘皆優恤。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, Shichang was given the posthumous name Zhuangjie and the others were all generously compensated.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned of his death, Shichang was given the posthumous name Zhuangjie (Stalwart Integrity), and the others were all generously compensated.

sentences.zh: 世昌既死，諸船或沉或逃，遂不復成軍。

translations.literal: After Shichang's death, the various ships were either sunk or fled, and the fleet was never re-formed.
translations.idiomatic: After Shichang's death the remaining ships were sunk or fled, and the fleet never fought as a force again.

sentences.zh: 世昌臨戰以忠義相激勵，死狀尤烈，世與左寶貴並稱雙忠云。

translations.literal: Shichang before battle stirred his men with talk of loyalty and righteousness; his manner of death was especially fierce; the age paired him with Zuo Baogui as the "Two Loyal Ones."
translations.idiomatic: Before battle Shichang roused his men with appeals to loyalty and duty, and his death was especially heroic; he and Zuo Baogui were paired in their own day as the "Two Loyal Ones."

sentences.zh: 永昇等，忠義有傳。

translations.literal: Yongsheng and the others — their loyalty and righteousness have been handed down.
translations.idiomatic: Yongsheng and the others, too, have their own stories of loyal service.

sentences.zh: 劉步蟾，侯官人。

translations.literal: Liu Buchan, a man of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Buchan was a native of Houguan.

sentences.zh: 幼穎異，肄業福建船政學堂，卒業試第一。

translations.literal: In youth he was exceptionally bright; he studied at the Fujian Naval Academy and ranked first in the graduation examination.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was unusually gifted; he studied at the Fujian Naval Academy and took first place in the graduation examination.

sentences.zh: 隸建威船，徼循南北洋資實練。

translations.literal: He was attached to the Jianwei and patrolled the North and South Seas to gain practical training.
translations.idiomatic: He served aboard the Jianwei, patrolling the northern and southern seas to gain practical experience.

sentences.zh: 同治十一年，會考閩、廣駕駛生，复冠其曹。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi, in the joint examination of Fujian and Guangdong navigation students, he again ranked first in his class.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi, in the joint examination of Fujian and Guangdong navigation students, he again came first in his class.

sentences.zh: 自是巡歷海岸河港，所蒞輒用​​西法測量。

translations.literal: From then on, touring coastal harbors and river ports, wherever he went he used Western methods of surveying.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, as he toured the coasts and river ports, he surveyed every place he visited by Western methods.

sentences.zh: 台灣地勢、番部風土尤諳習，為圖說甚晰。

translations.literal: He was especially well versed in Taiwan's terrain and the customs of the aboriginal districts, and his illustrated accounts were very clear.
translations.idiomatic: He knew Taiwan's terrain and the ways of the aboriginal districts especially well, and his illustrated reports were models of clarity.

sentences.zh: 光緒改元，赴歐學槍砲、水雷諸技，還留福建，敘守備。

translations.literal: When the Guangxu reign began, he went to Europe to study artillery, mines, and related skills; on returning he remained in Fujian and was appointed garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangxu reign he went to Europe to study artillery, mines, and related skills; on his return he remained in Fujian and was appointed garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 以丁寶楨、李鴻章論薦，擢游擊，會辦北洋操防。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Ding Baozhen and Li Hongzhang, he was promoted to guerrilla officer and assisted in Beiyang training and coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Ding Baozhen and Li Hongzhang he was promoted to guerrilla officer and assigned to help organize Beiyang training and coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 十一年，赴德國購定遠艦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he went to Germany to purchase the Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he went to Germany to take delivery of the Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 維時海軍初立，借才異地，西人實為管帶，步蟾副之。

translations.literal: At that time the navy was newly established and had to borrow talent from abroad; Westerners actually served as commanders, with Buchan as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The navy was still new and had to rely on foreign expertise; Westerners actually commanded the ships, with Buchan as their deputy.

sentences.zh: 已而西人去，頗能舉其職。

translations.literal: Before long the Westerners left, and he was quite able to fulfill his duties.
translations.idiomatic: When the Westerners left, he proved fully capable of filling their role.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以參將赴歐領四快船歸，遷副將，賜號強勇巴圖魯，擢右翼總兵。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, as a major he went to Europe to bring back four fast cruisers; he was promoted to vice commander, granted the title Qiangyong Batulu, and advanced to right-wing commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, as a major, he went to Europe and brought back four fast cruisers; he was promoted to vice commander, granted the title Qiangyong Batulu, and made right-wing commander.

sentences.zh: 二十年，中日戰起，海軍浮泊大東溝。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when the Sino-Japanese War broke out, the navy lay at anchor in Dadonggou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, when war broke out between China and Japan, the fleet lay at anchor in Dadonggou.

sentences.zh: 日艦至，督攝諸藝士御之，鏖戰三時許，沉敵艦三艘，運送銘軍八營，得以乘間登岸。

translations.literal: When Japanese ships arrived, he directed all the gunners in resisting them; after fierce fighting of about three hours, three enemy ships were sunk; he transported eight battalions of the Ming army, enabling them to land by seizing an interval.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese came up, he directed the gun crews in their defense; after three hours of fierce fighting three enemy ships were sunk, and he covered the landing of eight battalions of Liu Mingchuan's army by holding the sea long enough for them to get ashore.

sentences.zh: 論功，晉記名提督，易其勇號曰格洪額。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to registered nominal provincial commander and his brave title was changed to Gehong'e.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was advanced to registered nominal provincial commander and his brave-title was changed to Gehong'e.

sentences.zh: 明年，戰威海，中彈死。

translations.literal: The next year, fighting at Weihai, he was struck by a shell and died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, fighting at Weihai, he was struck by a shell and killed.

sentences.zh: 步蟾通西學，海軍規制多出其手。

translations.literal: Buchan was versed in Western learning, and much of the navy's regulations came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Buchan was thoroughly versed in Western learning, and much of the navy's regulations were of his drafting.

sentences.zh: 顧喜引用鄉人，視統帥丁汝昌蔑如也，時論責其不能和衷，致僨事。

translations.literal: Yet he liked to employ men from his home district and looked down on the commander-in-chief Ding Ruchang; contemporary opinion blamed him for failing to work in harmony and thereby bringing on disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he favored fellow provincials and treated Admiral Ding Ruchang with contempt; contemporaries blamed him for refusing to cooperate with his commander, which helped bring on defeat.

sentences.zh: 然華人明海戰術，步蟾為最先，雖敗挫，殺敵甚眾。

translations.literal: Yet among Chinese who understood naval tactics, Buchan was foremost; though defeated, he killed very many of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet among Chinese who truly understood naval warfare, Buchan was the first; though the fleet was beaten, he killed a great many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其忠烈，詔優恤。

translations.literal: The throne praised his loyalty and valor and ordered generous compensation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne honored his loyal death and ordered generous compensation for his family.

sentences.zh: 其左翼總兵林泰曾，亦籍侯官，同為船政學堂卒業生。

translations.literal: His left-wing commander Lin Taiceng was also registered in Houguan and was likewise a graduate of the Naval Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His left-wing commander Lin Taiceng was also a native of Houguan and a fellow graduate of the Naval Academy.

sentences.zh: 管鎮遠，戰大東溝，發砲敏捷，士卒用命，撲救火彈甚力，機營砲位無少損，賜號霍春助巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He commanded the Zhenyuan; at the battle of Dadonggou he fired with agility, his soldiers obeyed orders, he fought hard to extinguish incendiary shells, and the engine-room gun positions suffered no damage; he was granted the title Huochunzhu Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Commanding the Zhenyuan at Dadonggou, he fired with speed and precision; his crew obeyed without flinching and fought hard to put out incendiary shells, so that the engine-room batteries were scarcely touched; he was granted the title Huochunzhu Batulu.

sentences.zh: 駛還威海，艦觸礁受傷，憤恨蹈海死。

translations.literal: Sailing back to Weihai, the ship struck a reef and was damaged; in anger and shame he threw himself into the sea and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to Weihai his ship struck a reef and was damaged; in shame and fury he threw himself into the sea and drowned.

sentences.zh: 副將左翼中營游擊楊用霖、廣東大鵬協右營守備黃祖蓮並殉焉。

translations.literal: Vice Commander and left-wing central battalion guerrilla officer Yang Yonglin and Guangdong Dapeng Brigade right battalion garrison commander Huang Zulian also died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yonglin, guerrilla officer of the left-wing central battalion, and Huang Zulian, garrison commander of the Guangdong Dapeng Brigade's right battalion, died with him as well.

sentences.zh: 優恤各如製。

translations.literal: Generous compensation was granted to each according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Each was generously compensated according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 祖蓮等，忠義有傳。

translations.literal: Zulian and the others — their loyalty and righteousness have been handed down.
translations.idiomatic: Zulian and the others, too, have their own stories of loyal service.

sentences.zh: 戴宗騫，字孝侯，安徽壽州人。

translations.literal: Dai Zongqian, courtesy name Xiaohou, a native of Shouzhou in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zongqian, styled Xiaohou, was a native of Shouzhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 少以廩生治鄉團，捻酋苗沛霖數陷州，宗騫潛結各圩寨以攜貳其黨。

translations.literal: In youth, as a licentiate he organized local militia; the Nian chieftain Miao Peilin repeatedly seized the prefecture; Zongqian secretly won over the various stockaded hamlets to divide his followers.
translations.idiomatic: As a young licentiate he organized local militia; when the Nian chieftain Miao Peilin repeatedly seized the prefecture, Zongqian secretly won over the surrounding stockaded villages and turned Miao's own followers against him.

sentences.zh: 同治初，謁李鴻章，上平捻十策，深器之，遂留參戎幕，積勳至知縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi he called on Li Hongzhang and presented ten strategies for pacifying the Nian; Hongzhang greatly valued him and kept him on the military staff, where he accumulated merit until he reached the rank of magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign he sought out Li Hongzhang and presented ten strategies for pacifying the Nian; Hongzhang was deeply impressed and kept him on his staff, where he rose by merit to magistrate.

sentences.zh: 十一年，治南運河堤工。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he supervised dikes on the Southern Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he supervised dike works on the Southern Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 時畿輔興水利，計臣慮餉詘，議裁兵。

translations.literal: At that time water conservancy was being promoted in the capital region; the finance minister, fearing short revenue, proposed cutting troops.
translations.idiomatic: Water conservancy was then being promoted around the capital, but the finance minister, fearing a shortfall in revenue, proposed cutting the army.

sentences.zh: 宗騫上書，略謂：「津沽為九河故道，漳、衛交匯，水菑衍溢。

translations.literal: Zongqian submitted a memorial, stating in summary: "Jingu is the old channel of the Nine Rivers; the Zhang and Wei rivers meet here, and floodwaters spread far and wide.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqian submitted a memorial arguing, in brief: "The Tianjin area lies in the old channel of the Nine Rivers, where the Zhang and Wei meet and floods spread without check.

sentences.zh: 宜闢減河洩其勢，澌枝河分其漲，俾淮、練軍治之，則兵農合一，事半而功倍。」

translations.literal: Relief channels should be opened to release the force of the waters, and branch streams cut to divide the flood; let the Huai and Lian armies manage this, and soldier and farmer will be united — half the effort, double the result."
translations.idiomatic: Relief channels should be cut to release the pressure, and branch streams opened to divide the flood; put the Huai and Lian armies to the work, and soldier and farmer will be one — half the labor, twice the gain."

sentences.zh: 鴻章以其議上聞，遂命董其役，成稻田六萬餘畝。

translations.literal: Hongzhang reported his proposal to the throne and ordered him to direct the project; more than sixty thousand mu of paddy fields were brought into cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang forwarded the proposal to the throne and put Zongqian in charge of the project; more than sixty thousand mu of paddy were brought under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 箸海上屯田志紀其事。

translations.literal: He wrote the Record of Coastal Garrison Farms to commemorate the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He recorded the undertaking in his Record of Coastal Garrison Farms.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，中俄失和，吳大澂被命佐吉林邊務，奏宗騫自隨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu, when China and Russia fell out, Wu Dacheng was ordered to assist in Jilin border affairs and memorialized that Zongqian accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Guangxu, when relations with Russia broke down, Wu Dacheng was ordered to assist in Jilin border affairs and memorialized that Zongqian accompany him.

sentences.zh: 大澂兼攝屯政，宗騫為治道路，築砲台，設江防，徙直、東流民，假予產業，分部護之。

translations.literal: Dacheng also took charge of garrison-farm administration; Zongqian built roads, erected forts, set up river defenses, moved refugees from Zhili and the east, lent them property, and stationed guards by division to protect them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu also took charge of frontier colonization; Zongqian built roads, erected forts, organized river defenses, resettled refugees from Zhili and the east, lent them land and tools, and posted guards to protect them by district.

sentences.zh: 塞外灌莽千里，馬賊為民患，宗騫曰：「此屯政蠹也！」

translations.literal: Beyond the passes, scrub and marsh stretched for a thousand li, and mounted bandits plagued the people; Zongqian said: "This is the bane of garrison colonization!
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the passes scrubland stretched for a thousand li, and mounted bandits preyed on the settlers; Zongqian said, "This is the ruin of our colonization work!

sentences.zh: 率將士步馳八九百里，獲渠率王林等駢誅之。

translations.literal: He led officers and men on foot and horse for eight or nine hundred li, captured the ringleaders Wang Lin and others, and executed them all together.
translations.idiomatic: He led his officers and men on a march of eight or nine hundred li, captured the ringleaders Wang Lin and others, and put them all to death.

sentences.zh: 又以緣邊荒墾，戶籍殘耗，客民渙居不相顧，因令屯聚一處，略仿內地保甲，杜絕姦宄。

translations.literal: Moreover, because the borderlands were newly opened to cultivation and household registers were depleted, migrant settlers lived scattered and did not look out for one another; he therefore ordered them to cluster in one place, roughly imitating the interior baojia system, to cut off villainy.
translations.idiomatic: Because the frontier was newly opened and population registers were thin, migrant settlers lived scattered and could not protect one another; he ordered them to cluster together and organized them roughly on the interior baojia model to shut out crime.

sentences.zh: 復設製造局、採金廠，行之期年，商民輻湊。

translations.literal: He also established an arsenal and gold-mining works; after a year in operation, merchants and commoners gathered in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He also set up an arsenal and gold works; within a year merchants and settlers were flocking in.

sentences.zh: 大澂上其績狀，遷知府。

translations.literal: Dacheng reported his achievements and he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Wu reported his achievements and he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 八年，徙防洋、蒲河兩海口。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was transferred to defend the two harbors of Fangyang and Puhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to defend the harbors of Fangyang and Puhe.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂歸，鴻章疏留，宗騫請終制，弗許。

translations.literal: When his mother died he returned home in mourning; Hongzhang memorialized to retain him; Zongqian asked to complete the full mourning period but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he went home to mourn; Hongzhang memorialized to keep him in service; Zongqian asked to complete the full mourning period but was refused.

sentences.zh: 時興海軍，練水師，闢軍港，檄防威海。

translations.literal: At that time the navy was being built up, the fleet trained, a naval base opened, and he was ordered by dispatch to defend Weihai.
translations.idiomatic: The navy was then being built up, the fleet trained, and a naval base established; he was ordered by dispatch to take charge of the defenses at Weihai.

sentences.zh: 十三年，詣軍所，壁金線頂山，分鞏軍駐南岸，綏軍駐北岸。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he went to the garrison, fortified Jinxian Peak, and stationed the Gong army on the south bank and the Sui army on the north bank.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he took up his post, fortified Jinxian Peak, and posted the Gong army on the south bank and the Sui army on the north.

sentences.zh: 明年，建兩岸海台各三，南曰趙北嘴、鹿角嘴、龍廟嘴，北曰北山嘴、黃泥崖、祭祀台。

translations.literal: The next year, three coastal batteries were built on each shore: on the south, Zhaobeizui, Lujiaozui, and Longmiaozui; on the north, Beishanzui, Huangniya, and Jisitai.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he built three coastal batteries on each shore: on the south, Zhaobeizui, Lujiaozui, and Longmiaozui; on the north, Beishanzui, Huangniya, and Jisitai.

sentences.zh: 後路分築陸台四，南岸口較闊，更建日島地阱砲台，屹然為東防重鎮。

translations.literal: Four land batteries were built in the rear; the southern mouth was wider, and a masked battery was additionally built on Rijiao; the place stood firm as the great eastern defensive stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: Four land batteries were added in the rear; because the southern entrance was wider, he also built a masked battery on Rijiao Island, making Weihai a formidable eastern bastion.

sentences.zh: 十七年，校閱海軍禮成，論功晉道員。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when the naval review ceremonies were completed, he was promoted to circuit intendant for merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, after the naval review ceremonies were completed, he was promoted to circuit intendant for his services.

sentences.zh: 威海地瘠，士氣衰，更斥貲立義塾，延名師，至是始聞謳誦聲。

translations.literal: Weihai's land was poor and local morale had declined; he further spent his own funds to establish a charitable school and invited famous teachers; only then did the sound of chanting lessons begin to be heard.
translations.idiomatic: Weihai was a poor, dispirited place; he spent his own money to found a charitable school and hire distinguished teachers, and for the first time the sound of students reciting their lessons was heard there.

sentences.zh: 二十年夏，日艦來攻，率師御之，傷其艦四艘，再至再敗之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twentieth year, Japanese warships came to attack; he led his troops to resist, damaged four of their ships, and when they came again defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twentieth year Japanese warships attacked; he led the defense, damaged four enemy ships, and beat them back again when they returned.

sentences.zh: 既而旅順、大連相繼淪沒，威海勢益孤，電請北洋、山東益師，久弗應。

translations.literal: Before long Lüshun and Dalian fell in succession; Weihai's position grew more isolated; he telegraphed the Beiyang and Shandong commands for reinforcements, but for a long time received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Then Lüshun and Dalian fell in turn, leaving Weihai ever more isolated; he telegraphed Beiyang and Shandong for reinforcements, but for a long time received no answer.

sentences.zh: 其冬，連失文登、寧海。

translations.literal: That winter, Wendeng and Ninghai were lost in succession.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Wendeng and Ninghai fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 時宗騫守北岸，分統劉超佩守南岸，宗騫與約，寇至互相應。

translations.literal: At that time Zongqian held the north bank and the sub-commander Liu Chaopei held the south bank; Zongqian agreed with him that when the enemy came they would support each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqian held the north bank while sub-commander Liu Chaopei held the south; they agreed to support each other when the enemy came.

sentences.zh: 歲除，大風雪，戰橋頭集，綏軍大困，銳身救之出。

translations.literal: On New Year's Eve, in heavy wind and snow, fighting broke out at Qiaotouji; the Sui army was in great distress, and he boldly went in person to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve, in a driving snowstorm, fighting broke out at Qiaotouji; the Sui army was hard pressed, and he went in person to bring them out.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，日軍至，輒敗去，折而南。

translations.literal: After the new year, Japanese troops arrived, were repeatedly beaten off, then turned south.
translations.idiomatic: After the new year Japanese troops came up, were beaten back again and again, then turned south.

sentences.zh: 宗騫往援，而超佩蹌踉遁，三台拱手讓敵，反訴巡撫李秉衡，誣宗騫背約。

translations.literal: Zongqian went to their aid, but Chaopei fled in disorder; the three batteries were surrendered to the enemy without a fight; he instead reported to Governor Li Bingheng, falsely accusing Zongqian of breaking their agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqian went to help, but Chaopei fled in disorder and surrendered three batteries without a fight; he then reported to Governor Li Bingheng, falsely accusing Zongqian of breaking their agreement.

sentences.zh: 宗騫抗辯，願復三台贖罪。

translations.literal: Zongqian protested in defense and offered to recover the three batteries to atone for his fault.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqian defended himself and offered to retake the three batteries to atone for the loss.

sentences.zh: 乃募敢死士奪還二台，唯龍廟嘴未復。

translations.literal: He then recruited dare-to-die men and recaptured two batteries; only Longmiaozui was not recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a band of volunteers and recaptured two of the batteries; only Longmiaozui remained in enemy hands.

sentences.zh: 日軍倏大集，二台仍不守，宗騫退歸，登祭祀台。

translations.literal: Japanese troops suddenly gathered in force; the two batteries still could not be held; Zongqian withdrew and mounted Jisitai.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese suddenly massed in force; the two batteries could not be held; Zongqian fell back and took his stand on Jisitai.

sentences.zh: 所部卒譁變，宗騫佯弗省，行數武，槍齊發，材官追斬一人，眾散走。

translations.literal: His troops mutinied; Zongqian pretended not to notice; after he had walked a few paces, guns fired together; a sergeant pursued and beheaded one man, and the crowd scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: His troops mutinied; Zongqian pretended not to notice; after he had walked a few paces the mutineers opened fire together; a sergeant ran one man down and cut off his head, and the rest scattered.

sentences.zh: 宗騫既登，乃無一從者。

translations.literal: Once Zongqian had mounted the battery, not a single man followed him.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Zongqian reached the battery, not a single man was still with him.

sentences.zh: 夜宿藥庫，丁汝昌詣籌戰守策，宗騫曰：「綏、鞏軍已西去，孤台危棘，恐資敵。」

translations.literal: That night he lodged in the powder magazine; Ding Ruchang came to discuss attack and defense; Zongqian said: "The Sui and Gong armies have already gone west; this isolated battery is in peril and may only supply the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: That night he slept in the powder magazine; Ding Ruchang came to discuss strategy, and Zongqian said, "The Sui and Gong armies have already gone west; this isolated battery is untenable and will only arm the enemy."

sentences.zh: 汝昌令毀台，強掖之下。

translations.literal: Ruchang ordered the battery destroyed and forcibly helped him down.
translations.idiomatic: Ruchang ordered the battery destroyed and had him brought down by force.

sentences.zh: 宗騫念南北各有地阱台，此其勢尚可為，乃詣劉公島就副將張德山。

translations.literal: Zongqian reflected that north and south each had masked batteries and the situation could still be managed; he therefore went to Liugong Island to see Vice Commander Zhang Deshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqian thought that with masked batteries on both shores the defense might still be saved, and went to Liugong Island to see Vice Commander Zhang Deshan.

sentences.zh: 德山無戰守志，宗騫飲金死，威海師遂熸。

translations.literal: Deshan had no will to fight or hold; Zongqian took poison and died, and the Weihai forces were extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Deshan had no stomach for a fight; Zongqian took poison and died, and the Weihai garrison was lost.

sentences.zh: 鴻章以死事聞，詔優恤。

translations.literal: Hongzhang reported his death in service, and the throne ordered generous compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang reported his death in service, and the throne ordered generous compensation.

sentences.zh: 復以秉衡請，贈太常寺卿。

translations.literal: On Bingheng's further petition, he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On Bingheng's further petition, he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 論曰：中東之戰，陸軍皆遁，寶貴獨死平壤；

translations.literal: The historian comments: In the China–Japan War, the land armies all fled, but Baogui alone died at Pyongyang;
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In the war with Japan, the land armies all fled, but Baogui alone died at Pyongyang;

sentences.zh: 海軍皆降，世昌獨死東溝。

translations.literal: the navy all surrendered, but Shichang alone died at Dadonggou.
translations.idiomatic: the navy all surrendered, but Shichang alone died at Dadonggou.

sentences.zh: 中外傳其壯節，並稱「雙忠」。

translations.literal: Within and beyond the realm their heroic deaths were told, and they were jointly called the "Two Loyal Ones."
translations.idiomatic: Their heroic deaths were celebrated far and wide, and the two were paired as the "Two Loyal Ones."

sentences.zh: 及日兵入奉，永山獨死鳳城，敵遂長驅進矣。

translations.literal: When Japanese troops entered Fengtian, Yong Shan alone died at Fengcheng, and the enemy then drove deep inland.
translations.idiomatic: When Japanese troops entered Fengtian, Yong Shan alone died at Fengcheng, and the enemy drove on unchecked.

sentences.zh: 旅、大既失，威海勢孤，步蟾、宗騫皆先後誓死。

translations.literal: After Lüshun and Dalian were lost, Weihai stood isolated; Buchan and Zongqian each in turn swore to die.
translations.idiomatic: After Lüshun and Dalian fell, Weihai was cut off; Buchan and Zongqian each in turn swore to die for the cause.

sentences.zh: 士氣如此，豈遂不可一戰？

translations.literal: With morale such as this, could they truly not have fought one more battle?
translations.idiomatic: With spirit like this in the ranks, could they really not have fought once more?

sentences.zh: 此主兵者之責。

translations.literal: This was the responsibility of those who commanded the armies.
translations.idiomatic: That failure lay with those who commanded the armies.

sentences.zh: 五人雖敗，猶有榮焉！

translations.literal: Though these five men were defeated, they still had honor!
translations.idiomatic: Though these five men were defeated, they died with honor!
